Over four rounds, each player draws colored metro lines on their own map, starting from two designated departure stations on opposite sides of the city. As Station cards are revealed, everyone simultaneously extends their current line to matching symbols, carefully following the printed connections and strict building rules—no crossing tracks, no loops, and no retracing your path. [Rating: 3/10] Take a simple premise and make it increasingly complicated to the point where it's just not fun anymore. I find this version both finicky and limiting. Would much rather play Next Station: Paris (which I think is the best version of this game series)

[Rating: 5/10] This is for me a school example of taking it one step too far, which results in totally killing the clean original design which made Next Station: London a success. The 2 sides of Berlin make it simply too complicated and the squares you have to draw aroun stations make it too hard to see and not forget stations with multiple colors.

[Rating: 6/10] It's fine?  I still prefer the original to this one where you have two separate tracks for each color and a bonus is awarded if you can join them together.

[Rating: 6/10] Making games in this system more complicated does not make them better. I think I've liked each new one less than the one before. This one is different enough that maybe I'll change my mind if I play more but why not just play the original?

[Rating: 7/10] The new Next Station in the series is Berlin. I'll rate this the same as all the others because it pretty much plays the same as the previous three. The unique thing with Berlin is your paper is split in half with the same colored starting station on each side. When a card is revealed you must extend the track that starts on the specific side of your sheet with a point bonus for linking up the two tracks from each side. Once all cards of a specific side have been played then you switch colors. Like I said nothing completely new or different here with Berlin, but another solid spin with the Nex

[Rating: 7/10] Another goot Next Station game, with new twists, but not as simple and good as London.
